results.title: Air Travel Demand Elasticities
results.content: This document reports the findings of a review of the economics and business literature on empirically-estimated own-price elasticities of demand for air travel for Canada and other major developed countries. Accordingly, to examine the sensitivity of the demand for air travel to its price, separate estimates of the own-price elasticity of demand are gathered for each of these distinct markets. Standardized information on 21 Canadian and international empirical studies of own-price elasticities of demand for air travel is provided in this report. A scoring system based on desirable characteristics of demand studies is applied to each of the 21 studies to improve the level of confidence regarding the practical use of own-price elasticity values in assessing air travel demand. For example, values for the own-price elasticity of demand for long-haul domestic leisure are based on six estimates from two studies. The purpose of this study is to report on all or most of the economics and business literature dealing with empirically estimated demand functions for air travel and to collect a range of fare elasticity measures for air travel and provide some judgment as to which elasticity values would be more representative of the true values to be found in different markets in Canada. This implies that ideally, empirical studies of air travel demand should separate business and leisure travellers or at least be able to include some information on booking times in order to account for this price discrimination, and that price data should be calibrated for inter-temporal price discrimination: for example, the use of full-fare economy class ticket prices as data will overestimate the absolute value of the price elasticity coefficient. * Elasticity and Air Travel No ratings yet Elasticity and Air Travel 52 pages. * Estimating Air Travel Demand Elasticities Final Report No ratings yet Estimating Air Travel Demand Elasticities Final Report 58 pages. * Air Travel Demand Elasticities No ratings yet Air Travel Demand Elasticities 58 pages. * Demand For Air Travel: Eva Endrizalová Němec Vladimír No ratings yet Demand For Air Travel: Eva Endrizalová Němec Vladimír 3 pages. * Price Elasticity of Demand Guide 88% (8) Price Elasticity of Demand Guide 31 pages.

results.title: Oil price elasticities and oil price fluctuations - ScienceDirect
results.content: Studies identifying oil shocks using structural vector autoregressions (VARs) reach different conclusions on the relative importance of supply and demand factors in explaining oil market fluctuations. When the estimated elasticities are embedded into a structural VAR, supply and demand shocks play an equally important role in explaining oil prices and oil quantities. In particular, with a configuration of the oil market characterized by a zero supply elasticity, all movements in oil prices are attributed to oil-specific demand shocks. By contrast, setting the supply elasticity to 0.1 implies that oil supply and oil demand shocks are equally important drivers of oil price fluctuations. This section provides empirical evidence about the price elasticity of global supply and demand for crude oil by estimating instrumental variable (IV) panel regressions. Using external information from a large panel of countries, we impose restrictions on the short-run price elasticities of oil supply and oil demand in order to identify a structural VAR model of the global oil market.
